thresholds.caution: Equal to the lowest weight, so any risk signal alone gives at least caution. Measured: 0 of 625 legitimate samples outside hosting pages, near-neighbour names, and names that contain a brand reach it.
thresholds.danger: Signals that prove an imitation alone (70 or more) reach it alone; a typo-distance match (60) and a brand name beside a neutral word (40) do not, because real names exist there. Measured: 2 of 760 legitimate samples reach it, both accepted exceptions, and 67 of 121 covered phishing samples do.

weights.homograph/letters-one: Imitating a protected domain with lookalike characters has no innocent use, so it reaches danger alone. Measured: 6 phishing samples trigger it, 0 of 760 legitimate ones, including 24 internationalized domains and 368 real pages of protected domains.
weights.homograph/letters-many: Imitating a protected domain with lookalike characters has no innocent use, so it reaches danger alone. Measured: 9 phishing samples trigger it, 0 of 760 legitimate ones, including 24 internationalized domains and 368 real pages of protected domains.
weights.homograph/whole-script: Imitating a protected domain with lookalike characters has no innocent use, so it reaches danger alone. Measured: 2 phishing samples trigger it, 0 of 760 legitimate ones, including 24 internationalized domains and 368 real pages of protected domains.
weights.homograph/lookalike: Imitating a protected domain with lookalike characters has no innocent use, so it reaches danger alone. Measured: 10 phishing samples trigger it, 0 of 760 legitimate ones, including 24 internationalized domains and 368 real pages of protected domains.
weights.typosquat/changed: One letter away from a protected domain is how a typo domain looks, but real names sit there too, so it stays under danger and gives caution. Measured: 4 phishing samples and 15 legitimate ones, all at caution. Of 58 real names close to a protected domain, 25 trigger nothing; the rest are ordinary words one letter from a brand, such as cloud.com beside icloud.com.

weights.typosquat/ending: A protected name under a mistyped ending such as con.bo. Same weight as the other one-slip variants. Measured: 3 phishing samples, 0 legitimate ones.
weights.typosquat/two: Two slips are weaker evidence than one, so it gives caution with room to spare. Measured: 2 phishing samples, 0 legitimate ones.
weights.hosting/plain: Anyone can publish on these services, and most pages on them are honest, so the lowest weight that still shows a mark. Measured: 21 of 35 legitimate hosting samples and 3 phishing samples; none at danger.
weights.hosting/one-word: One lure word in the publisher's name is common in honest pages. Measured: 7 legitimate samples and 2 phishing samples, all at caution.
weights.hosting/two-words: Two lure words without a brand name appear in honest pages too, so it stays at caution. Measured: 2 legitimate samples and 2 phishing samples.
weights.hosting/words: Three lure words, or a brand name beside a lure word, is the shape of the real phishing email of 19 November 2026, so it reaches danger alone. Measured: 6 phishing samples, 2 of them real, and 2 constructed legitimate samples that are accepted exceptions.
weights.subdomain/domain: A whole protected domain at the start of another site's name has no innocent use. Measured: 11 phishing samples, 0 of 760 legitimate ones.
weights.subdomain/suffix: The state's ending inside another site's name, with no protected domain named: suspicious, not proof. Measured: 2 phishing samples, 0 legitimate ones.
weights.subdomain/suffix-lookalike: An ending that looks like the state's. A registry could hand it out honestly, so it gives caution. Measured: 2 phishing samples, 0 legitimate ones.
weights.mixed-script/one: A name that mixes alphabets has no innocent use in the corpus, so it reaches danger alone. Measured: 7 phishing samples, 0 of 760 legitimate ones.
weights.mixed-script/many: A name that mixes alphabets has no innocent use in the corpus, so it reaches danger alone. Measured: 7 phishing samples, 0 of 760 legitimate ones.
weights.mixed-script/several: A name that mixes alphabets has no innocent use in the corpus, so it reaches danger alone. Measured: 2 phishing samples, 0 of 760 legitimate ones.
weights.invisible-characters/host-one: A character nobody can see inside the name of the site, or in the text of the link, has no innocent use. Measured: 2 phishing samples, 0 of 394 legitimate ones.
weights.invisible-characters/host-many: A character nobody can see inside the name of the site, or in the text of the link, has no innocent use. Measured: 2 phishing samples, 0 of 394 legitimate ones.
weights.invisible-characters/text-one: A character nobody can see inside the name of the site, or in the text of the link, has no innocent use. Measured: 2 phishing samples, 0 of 394 legitimate ones.
weights.invisible-characters/text-many: A character nobody can see inside the name of the site, or in the text of the link, has no innocent use. Measured: 2 phishing samples, 0 of 394 legitimate ones.
weights.invisible-characters/link-one: An invisible character after the site's name can come from careless copying, so it gives caution. Measured: 2 phishing samples, 0 legitimate ones.
weights.invisible-characters/link-many: Same reading as one character: caution. Measured: 2 phishing samples, 0 legitimate ones.
weights.link-text-mismatch/brand: The text of the link shows a protected domain and the link leads to a site that is not that organization's, with a destination that can be read. It is the shape of the real phishing email of 25 November 2026, so it reaches danger alone. Measured on 2026-11-25: 5 phishing samples, 1 of them real, and 0 of 771 legitimate ones, 11 of which carry visible text, including two domains of one organization and an address shown on a link through a listed tracker.
weights.link-text-mismatch/other: The text shows a domain nobody protected owns and the link leads elsewhere. Unlisted tracking domains and sites that moved look the same, so it gives caution alone and reaches danger only beside another sign such as a free hosting page. Measured on 2026-11-25: 3 phishing samples at caution, 0 legitimate ones.
weights.credentials/decoy: A site's name written before the @ shows the intent to deceive, so it reaches danger alone. Measured: 3 phishing samples, 0 of 394 legitimate ones.
weights.credentials/plain: A user name before the @ is rare and legal; caution. Measured: 2 phishing samples, 0 legitimate ones.
weights.ip-host/encoded: A number written so that it does not look like an address hides the destination on purpose, but names no victim; high caution. Measured: 3 phishing samples, 0 legitimate ones.
weights.ip-host/public: A bare address is unusual for a public site and common in home and office equipment; caution. Measured: 2 phishing samples, 0 legitimate ones.
weights.encoded-host: Encoded letters in the site's name are unusual and prove nothing alone; the lowest weight that shows a mark. Measured: 3 phishing samples, 0 legitimate ones.
weights.combosquat/brand: A brand's name beside a neutral word is how a combination domain looks, but fan sites, resellers, and the brand's own extra domains look the same, so it gives caution and the text says it may be another site. Measured: 4 phishing samples and 2 legitimate ones (netflix-codes.com and paypal-community.com), all at caution.
weights.combosquat/lure: A brand's name beside a lure word such as «seguridad» or «verificar», in a domain that is not the brand's, is the shape of a phishing address, so it reaches danger alone. Measured: 11 phishing samples, 0 of 760 legitimate ones. Brands that are common words or short names trigger only in this variant.
